null-list.reason: The harness stores aNumberList as adversarial_number_list rows, one per element, so a null list and [] are both zero rows: a row sent to the PDP as null cannot be stored.

nul-in-string.reason: PostgreSQL text cannot hold a NUL character, so a row whose string holds one cannot be stored.

arithmetic/add/ternary-selecting-double-.reason: Same int() refusal as arithmetic/divide/int-truncates: SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL's int() conversion, so the addition over the ternary is never reached.

arithmetic/divide/field-by-field.reason: Cannot translate a division by a floating-point column or by computed arithmetic: its zero may be -0.0, which CEL divides a non-zero number into the opposite infinity from 0.0, while SQL compares -0.0 equal to 0.0 and has no portable way to read the sign bit. Divide by an integer or decimal column, or by a constant.

arithmetic/divide/int-by-list-index.reason: Same int() refusal as arithmetic/divide/int-truncates: SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL's int() conversion, so the int division over it is never reached.

arithmetic/divide/int-by-ternary.reason: Same int() refusal as arithmetic/divide/int-truncates: SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL's int() conversion, so the int division over it is never reached.

arithmetic/divide/negated-int-by-ternary.reason: Same int() refusal as arithmetic/divide/int-truncates: SQL CAST does not reproduce CEL's int() conversion, so the int division over it is never reached.

arithmetic/divide/negated-zero-divisor-l.reason: In is applied to a pair this adapter cannot read as one mapped operand against a constant list; the supported shapes are in(collection-attribute, [values]), in(map(collection, lambda), [values]) and in(attribute, collection-attribute).

arithmetic/divide/nested-division-diviso.reason: A division as the DIVISOR: the inner division can be a zero-denominator NaN or infinity, SQL has no literal for either, and against a column the sign of the result depends on that column. Refused rather than binding a non-finite double, which PostgreSQL orders above every number

arithmetic/divide/zero-divisor-in-list-l.reason: Cannot compare a column with a list() value: it builds a map or list, and a mapped column holds one scalar, which SQL equality cannot compare with either.

arithmetic/divide/zero-divisor-in-map-li.reason: Cannot compare a column with a struct() value: it builds a map or list, and a mapped column holds one scalar, which SQL equality cannot compare with either.

arithmetic/modulo/column-divisor-negativ.reason: mod is not supported in comparisons: CEL % is integer-only while attribute values are always doubles at check time, so a satisfiable policy must cast with int() first — and int() has no faithful SQL lowering, because CAST rounds where CEL truncates toward zero.

arithmetic/multiply/nan-times-zero-plus-.reason: arithmetic between a column and the NaN or infinity a zero denominator produces is not supported: SQL has no literal for either value, and neither folds to one constant against a column, because an infinity times or divided by a column depends on that column's sign. Compare the division itself, or keep the composition constant.

cast/double/malformed-string.reason: Cannot translate double(): SQL CAST reads the numeric prefix of a string where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, and PostgreSQL and MySQL round where CEL truncates toward zero, so the cast would admit rows the PDP denies.

cast/double/negated-malformed-string.reason: int() and double() over a string have no faithful SQL cast: CAST reads a numeric prefix where CEL requires the whole string and raises otherwise, and PostgreSQL and MySQL round where CEL truncates, so the negated cast would admit rows the PDP denies. Refused by the cast's own name

cast/string/from-integral-ternary.reason: Cannot translate string() over a computed value (a conversion, a ternary or a comparison): string() is lowered only over a mapped column, whose type decides CEL's spelling, and SQL CAST prints numbers and booleans differently from CEL ("1e+06", "true").

cast/string/from-negative-zero-double.reason: Cannot translate string() over a DoubleColumnType column: CEL renders a number as Go's shortest round-tripping form (1e+06, 2, -0) and no SQL CAST reproduces that for this column type, nor reads the sign of a stored -0.0. Text, integer and boolean columns are translatable, and a floating-point column only under == or != against a string literal other than "0" and "-0".

cast/string/from-ternary-with-int-branch.reason: Cannot translate string() over a computed value (a conversion, a ternary or a comparison): string() is lowered only over a mapped column, whose type decides CEL's spelling, and SQL CAST prints numbers and booleans differently from CEL ("1e+06", "true").

cast/string/negated-from-integral-ternar.reason: Cannot translate string() over a computed value (a conversion, a ternary or a comparison): string() is lowered only over a mapped column, whose type decides CEL's spelling, and SQL CAST prints numbers and booleans differently from CEL ("1e+06", "true").

cast/timestamp/malformed-string.reason: timestamp() comparison requires a column that stores an absolute instant — an exposed-java-time or exposed-kotlin-datetime timestamp() or timestampWithTimeZone() column — but 'request.resource.attr.createdBy' maps to a VarCharColumnType column. A local date-time, a date and a string are all ambiguous about which instant they hold; remap the column.

cast/timestamp/negated-malformed-string.reason: timestamp() needs a column that stores an absolute instant; createdBy is the varchar the corpus deliberately maps it to, and a string column is ambiguous about which instant it holds, so the conversion failure CEL raises for a malformed string has no SQL counterpart. Refused when the timestamp() operand is resolved

collection/add/literal-list-plus-attribu.reason: Cannot compare a column with a list() value: it builds a map or list, and a mapped column holds one scalar, which SQL equality cannot compare with either.

collection/except/as-lambda-body.reason: CEL needs a boolean where the dyn()-wrapped except() list stands, a no-overload error; the planner keeps the wrapper as operator `dyn`, which the adapter does not translate.

collection/except/as-whole-condition.reason: except() computes a list difference, which has no row-filter form: the result is a list, and its consumers here — size(), equality with a non-empty list, a root boolean, a principal list — would need the difference materialised. Only a difference compared with an empty list translates, as every element of the relation being in the removed list

collection/except/equals-list-literal.reason: except() computes a list difference, which has no row-filter form: the result is a list, and its consumers here — size(), equality with a non-empty list, a root boolean, a principal list — would need the difference materialised. Only a difference compared with an empty list translates, as every element of the relation being in the removed list

collection/except/negated-as-whole-condi.reason: CEL needs a boolean where the dyn()-wrapped except() list stands, a no-overload error; the planner keeps the wrapper as operator `dyn`, which the adapter does not translate.

collection/except/size-of-difference.reason: except() computes a list difference, which has no row-filter form: the result is a list, and its consumers here — size(), equality with a non-empty list, a root boolean, a principal list — would need the difference materialised. Only a difference compared with an empty list translates, as every element of the relation being in the removed list

collection/exists/map-keys.reason: `parent` is a to-one relation, which CEL reads as a map, and a macro over a map ranges over its keys: the attribute names present on the related row. A related row has no key set SQL can iterate, and the mapping declares no element column to stand for one, so the macro is refused when its collection is resolved

collection/exists/negated-map-keys.reason: Same refusal as collection/exists/map-keys, under negation: a macro over the to-one `parent` ranges over its attribute names, which SQL has no row to iterate

collection/exists/two-variable-index-and.reason: A two-variable comprehension binds a list index or a map key as its first variable, and no mapped column holds either: the rows a relation subquery returns carry no CEL list order to number, and an attribute mapping names columns, never the key set of a map. The lambda is refused for what it binds, before its range is resolved

collection/exists/two-variable-map-key-a.reason: A two-variable comprehension binds a list index or a map key as its first variable, and no mapped column holds either: the rows a relation subquery returns carry no CEL list order to number, and an attribute mapping names columns, never the key set of a map. The lambda is refused for what it binds, before its range is resolved

collection/filter/as-conjunct.reason: filter() returns a list, not a boolean, so it cannot be a condition on its own; only size(filter(...)) gives the list a scalar meaning

collection/filter/as-whole-condition.reason: filter() returns a list, not a boolean, so it cannot be a condition on its own; only size(filter(...)) gives the list a scalar meaning

collection/filter/size-of-ternary-over-f.reason: Size() is applied to a collection this adapter cannot reach as a table: its argument must be a mapped attribute or filter(collection, lambda).

collection/has-intersection/empty-litera.reason: The harness maps tags as a relation with no element column, so a bare hasIntersection over it is unmapped, even against an empty list.

collection/has-intersection/two-resource.reason: hasIntersection is translated only against a literal list, not between a stored collection and a map() projection.

collection/intersect/duplicates-in-short.reason: Cerbos's intersect() keeps duplicates from whichever list is shorter, so size(intersect(a, b)) depends on the two lists' lengths, which no SQL set operation or correlated count reproduces. intersect() is translated only compared with an empty list, where it is hasIntersection()

collection/map/as-whole-condition.reason: map() returns a list, not a boolean, so it cannot be a condition on its own; only hasIntersection(map(...), [...]) gives the list a scalar meaning

comparison/equals/list-holding-nan.reason: Cannot compare a column with a list() value: a mapped column holds one scalar, which SQL equality cannot compare with a list.

conditional/ternary/string-match-receive.reason: A ternary is distributed into its branches only as an operand of ==, !=, <, <=, > or >=; as the receiver of contains() it is refused.

hierarchy/overlaps/field-to-field.reason: Both hierarchies are read from columns, so there is no constant path to expand into prefixes, and an Exposed expression cannot split a column on a delimiter to compare it segment by segment.

logic/and/non-boolean-operand-in-value-n.reason: An and() whose result is compared with `==` as a value has no translation: the walker lowers and() only in condition position, and refuses it as an operand of eq.

logic/bare/list-attribute.reason: Request.resource.attr.aBoolList is mapped as a relation, but a condition needs a scalar column, so a list read as one is refused.

logic/not/bare-list-attribute.reason: Request.resource.attr.aBoolList is mapped as a relation, but a condition needs a scalar column, so a list read as one is refused.

membership/in/map-attribute-keys.reason: `parent` is a to-one relation, which CEL reads as a map, and `in` over a map tests its keys: the attribute names present on the related row. A related row has no key set SQL can test, and the mapping declares no element column to stand for one, so the membership is refused when its container is resolved

membership/in/negated-map-attribute-keys.reason: Same refusal as membership/in/map-attribute-keys, under negation: `in` over the to-one `parent` tests its attribute names, which SQL has no row to read

principal/all/left-unresolved-in-ternary.reason: The planner leaves the principal list unresolved in this ternary branch, so the plan names request.principal.attr.allowedTags, which is not a value the adapter can bind and not a field of any store. The adapter refuses the reference.

principal/except/size-after-removing-res.reason: except() computes a list difference, which has no row-filter form: the result is a list, and its consumers here — size(), equality with a non-empty list, a root boolean, a principal list — would need the difference materialised. Only a difference compared with an empty list translates, as every element of the relation being in the removed list

principal/filter/as-whole-condition.reason: CEL needs a boolean where the dyn()-wrapped filter() list stands, a no-overload error; the planner keeps the wrapper as operator `dyn`, which the adapter does not translate.

principal/map/as-whole-condition.reason: CEL needs a boolean where the dyn()-wrapped map() list stands, a no-overload error; the planner keeps the wrapper as operator `dyn`, which the adapter does not translate.

regex/matches/anchored-prefix-dot-star.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; a .* not followed by an end anchor is refused.

regex/matches/case-fold-perl-non-word-cl.reason: matches() is lowered only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly. Under (?i), \W is every character but the word characters and their case folds U+017F and U+212A, and LIKE has no character class.

regex/matches/case-insensitive-non-ascii.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; (?i) is spelled as ASCII case alternatives, so a non-ASCII letter under it is refused.

regex/matches/dot-all-flag.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; an inline flag other than a leading (?i) is refused.

regex/matches/end-anchor-mid-pattern.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; an anchor followed by more pattern is refused.

regex/matches/field-to-field.reason: matches() is compiled into LIKE at translation, so it is translated only against a constant pattern; a pattern read from a row is refused.

regex/matches/negated-class.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; a negated character class has no LIKE spelling and is refused.

regex/matches/negated-repeated-start-anc.reason: matches() is lowered only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly. RE2 reads the * after ^ as a repetition of the start anchor, which the regex lowering does not read, so ^*a$ is refused rather than lowered with a guess at what the * means.

regex/matches/non-digit-class.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; \D has no LIKE spelling and is refused.

regex/matches/repeated-start-anchor.reason: matches() is lowered only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly. RE2 reads the * after ^ as a repetition of the start anchor, which the regex lowering does not read, so ^*a$ is refused rather than lowered with a guess at what the * means.

regex/matches/unanchored-dot.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; a lone . would become _, which matches a newline RE2's . does not, so it is refused.

regex/matches/unanchored-quantifiers.reason: matches() is translated only where LIKE, = and REPLACE spell the RE2 pattern exactly: finite alternatives, anchored .* and .+, and ^[set]*$. An unbounded repetition of a literal (x*, a+) inside a pattern has no finite expansion and no LIKE wildcard that counts only one character's repeats, so it is refused when the pattern is compiled

regex/matches/unbounded-count.reason: matches() is translated only where LIKE, = and REPLACE spell the RE2 pattern exactly; the unbounded run `.{8,}` is lowered only as `.*` or `.+` between finite parts, so it is refused when the pattern is compiled

regex/matches/word-boundary.reason: No SQL engine implements RE2, so matches() lowers to LIKE only where LIKE can spell the pattern exactly; \b has no LIKE spelling and is refused.

size/greater-than/map-projection.reason: size() takes a mapped collection or a filter(); a map() projection is refused, since its body is evaluated per element and one erroring element (b6's unnamed tag) makes the count an error.

string/contains/nul-needle.reason: A needle holding a NUL character is refused on every store: PostgreSQL text cannot hold one, so binding it errors, and MySQL's LIKE stops reading the pattern at it.

timestamp/equals/field-to-field-without-.reason: Two instant columns compared WITHOUT timestamp(): CEL compares their RFC 3339 STRINGS, so one instant written two ways is unequal, while SQL compares instants. The operand-type guard refuses two temporal columns under a plain comparison

type-mismatch/in/string-field-in-string-.reason: `in` with an attribute haystack needs a relation mapping; aOptionalString is a scalar column, over which CEL raises a no-overload error.

type-mismatch/less-than/negated-nan-agai.reason: CEL compares values of different types without coercion — equality is a definite false and ordering a no-overload error — while SQL coerces one side (MySQL coerces the string column to a number). The operand-type guard compares the constant's or the other column's type with the mapped column's declared type and refuses a mismatch before any SQL is built

type-mismatch/string/number-list-attribu.reason: Request.resource.attr.aNumberList is mapped as a relation, but this position needs a scalar column.

type-mismatch/subtract/negated-string-mi.reason: Arithmetic over 'request.resource.attr.createdAt' requires a numeric column, but it maps to a JavaInstantColumnType column.
